summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and prior Puestow procedure was admitted for elective repair of a symptomatic incisional hernia that had caused a minor bowel obstruction. He underwent an uncomplicated open ventral incisional hernia repair with Prolene mesh overlay on hospital day one. Postoperatively, he was managed with IV fluids, antibiotics, a JP drain, and pain control via PCA initially, transitioning to oral medications. His diet was advanced from clear liquids on postoperative day one to a regular diet by day three. He voided independently after catheter removal, remained afebrile, and had stable vital signs. He was discharged home on postoperative day three with instructions for incision and drain care, oral Keflex, and follow-up. His chronic conditions, including hypertension, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and diabetes, were managed with continuation of most home medications.
problems: Incisional hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
